newsitem.title: USA: Dlr sturdy at US open, bulls favor gains vs Swiss.
newsitem.headline: Dlr sturdy at US open, bulls favor gains vs Swiss.

text.p: The dollar started on solid ground with bulls increasingly focusing their appetites on the surging dollar/Swiss, amid nagging worries that the Bundesbank may try to stem the mark's slide, dealers said.
Versus marks, the dollar barely exceeded Thursday's 6-year high at 1.84, while the tumbling Swiss propelled the dollar past 1.51 to 1.5176 Swiss in European dealings.
"After the move up yesterday in dollar/Swiss, I think for dollar bulls that is obviously yet another positive development," said Bob Lynch, currency strategist at Paribas Corp.
"There is probably some opportunity for dollar/mark to consolidate, maybe stall a little bit at least temporarily," Lynch continued.

The dollar opened at 1.8370/75 marks, up from 1.8322/32 at Thursday's close, but off its 1.8403 overnight peak. Dollar/Swiss was up at 1.5135/45, compared with Thursday's last quote of 1.5053/63. Dollar/yen was flat at 116.05/15.

Thursday's strength against the mark spilled over into early Friday, with the dollar getting some extra support from talk that a French finance official said it would not be a surprise to see 2.00 marks per dollar.
But the Bundesbank meeting on Thursday seemed to generate more questions about its views on the strengthening dollar than it answered, and traders' caution eventually checked the dollar's advance.

In Friday's Handelsblatt newspaper, council member Reimut Jochimsen said the central bank's decision to hold its repo rate at a fixed 3.0 percent for two weeks showed the Bundesbank was "driving carefully" in view of the weak mark.
The Bundesbanker seemed to be signalling they were leaving their options open while on a four-week summer recess, dealers said.

"There is a little fear that maybe the Bundesbank is on the verge of doing something ... Jochimsen made some comments as well as some other people," said James Powers, a vice president of corporate foreign exchange at Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale.

Tepid jawboning to date has done little to derail dollar/mark, which seems destined to try the 1991 high of 1.8430 soon, unless the Germans increase interest rates or invervene directly, dealers said.
But given the surging mark/Swiss, dollar/mark is seen lagging dollar/Swiss, which hit a 47-month high on Friday.
The mark extended its gains to 0.8262 Swiss overnight, sapping strength from dollar/mark, after jumping a bit more than a centime on Thursday amid talk of fund and options-related buying.
The dollar initially shrugged off a 2.3 percent jump in June U.S. durable goods orders, although the number was above the 1.4 percent rise expected.
In other trade, the dollar edged up to Canadian $1.3819/24 from C$1.3815/20.
The pound fell to $1.6640/50 from $1.6750/60 and the Australian dollar rose to $0.7373/78 from $0.7360/65.
